saints.name: St. Sabbas
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: A father of Eastern monasticism who founded the Great Lavra above the Kidron valley and defended the faith of Chalcedon…
biography: Sabbas was born in Cappadocia in 439 and as a young man went to Palestine, where he embraced the monastic life under St. Euthymius. In 483 he founded in the desert gorge near Jerusalem the Great Lavra, later called Mar Saba, which became the most famous monastery of the Holy Land and endures to this day.

Widely revered for holiness and wisdom, he was sent twice to Constantinople to plead the cause of orthodoxy and of his people, and he upheld the Council of Chalcedon against its opponents. He died at the Lavra in 532.
saints.knownFor: Founder of the Great Lavra (Mar Saba) and father of Palestinian monasticism.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 5 December
